scope: R202: source-level confirmation that consecutive encoder calls re-transfer 63 GB each, giving a no-maths-change fix for the encoder under-2s target

confirms_r201b_premise.previous_status: inferred from the numerical coincidence 63 GB / 3.047 s = 20.7 GB/s against the measured 20.0 GB/s H2D bandwidth
confirms_r201b_premise.evidence: _encode_text_hidden (pipeline_minimax_h3.py:1438) has three paths; the manual component offload path wraps the call in `with self._component_on_device(self.text_encoder)`, which loads on entry and offloads on exit, so every encode_prompt call transfers the full 63 GB

core_new_finding.code: hidden = self.encode_prompt(prepared) then a loop appending self.encode_prompt(...) for prompts[1:]
core_new_finding.observation: the N encoder calls run back to back with nothing between them, and the DiT has not started yet
core_new_finding.implication: there is no reason to re-transfer the weights between these calls, yet the current implementation does exactly that

fix.shape: wrap all N calls in a single residency window
fix.saves: (N-1) x 63 GB of transfer, about (N-1) x 3.05 s
fix.math_impact: none: the computation is identical, so this satisfies the keep-original-maths requirement for the encoder direction
fix.note: c is pure compute, roughly 0.17-0.6 s by the compute roofline

additional_mechanism: _prepare_local_conditioning also has a reuse_text branch that reuses already-encoded hidden states instead of recomputing, so upstream could avoid even the repeated encoding
open_questions: what is N exactly; R136s wording of three requests suggests 3 but it was not confirmed
which of the three paths is actually taken, which depends on the engines offload configuration
note_these_are_answerable: both can be checked from existing receipts or configuration without running the model
methodology_improvement: after three consecutive compute-first errors (R189, R199, R199-C), R201b flagged the premise as unverified and this round confirmed it directly from source; the conclusion now rests on code rather than on a numerical coincidence

same_round_correction.issue: the residency-window fix proposed above does not apply because N=1 in the measured path
same_round_correction.evidence: grep for 'encoding continuation prompt' across the R126 logs returns nothing, and pipeline_minimax_h3.py:2409 logs that line before every continuation prompt; no hit means len(prompts)==1, so N=1
same_round_correction.consequence: with a single call there is no repeated transfer to eliminate, so the fix yields zero benefit and is withdrawn
same_round_correction.what_r136_meant: the 'three requests' were probably three separate benchmark requests, not three prompts inside one request; those are entirely different because separate requests do not involve consecutive repeat transfers
same_round_correction.also_clarified: per_block_cpu_offload_used and --offload native refer to DiT per-block CPU offload, not text encoder residency; I had conflated the two

real_remaining_paths_with_N1.path: keep the encoder resident across requests
real_remaining_paths_with_N1.obstacle: memory: DiT at TP2 is about 31 GB per rank plus encoder 7.9 GB per rank equals 38.9 GB, above 32 GB, but DiT uses per-block offload so its steady-state footprint may be far below 31 GB and the actual peak must be measured

real_remaining_paths_with_N1.path: reduce the transferred volume, for example a smaller dtype copy
real_remaining_paths_with_N1.obstacle: changes numerics, violating keep-original-maths and requiring approval

real_remaining_paths_with_N1.path: speed up the transfer itself, pinned memory or a wider H2D path
real_remaining_paths_with_N1.detail: R198 measured 20.0 GB/s pinned against 9.7 GB/s unpinned for large tensors, a 2.06x difference; if the encoder load currently walks an unpinned path, switching would take the 63 GB load from the 6.5 s class down to the 3.15 s class

cheapest_likely_path: pinning: confirm and fix the memory pin state of the encoder load; this needs no maths change and could alone bring the encoder under 2 s
